Why this stop is raised after the rejected earlier stop (`2026-11-19T15:16:25Z`): both the text changed to embed the operator's earlier local-calibration boundary (lines 10, 14, 26, 58) and local fixes (lines 12, 18, 20-23, 32, 37, 39), AND the new depth-1 reports present a new case the operator's earlier reason does not address (O(1) concrete marginal-anchor injection, which compares concrete tasks in local scope without a numeric common scale) alongside new tensions introduced by the post-rejection edits.

Unsupported/refuted claims requiring rewrite (all Defect):
1. Universal claim, abstract-bar vs. global-view dichotomy, and "small workload" boundary defeated by concrete marginal-anchor injection (lines 10, 14, 26, 30, 58, 66) — Defect (`kb/reports/state/review/results/kb/theory/context-isolation-for-focus-conflicts-with-global-prioritization.md/kb/instructions/critique-note.md`; `kb/reports/state/review/results/kb/theory/context-isolation-for-focus-conflicts-with-global-prioritization.md/kb/instructions/premise-decomposition-gate.md`; `kb/reports/state/review/results/kb/theory/context-isolation-for-focus-conflicts-with-global-prioritization.md/kb/instructions/composition-friction-gate.md`; `kb/reports/state/review/results/kb/theory/context-isolation-for-focus-conflicts-with-global-prioritization.md/semantic/explanatory-reach.md`): the claim that without a locally calibrated numeric scale no compact injected signal is locally comparable—so concrete side-by-side comparison requires a separate wide-shallow global view (line 26) and comparison-sufficient live state fits in-window only on a small workload (line 58)—is false for concrete marginal-anchor injection (injecting a ~50-300 token live card naming the 1-5 concrete competing tasks at the current priority cutoff). That anchor requires no numeric scale, enables side-by-side comparison of concrete tasks in local scope, and scales as O(1) with the cutoff frontier rather than O(N) with portfolio size. Stipulating away working summaries inside Condition 2 makes Condition 2 outcome-insulated while punting its structural triggers (e.g., content-addressed cross-portfolio coupling, concurrent sibling-worker staleness, or attention interference) to Open Question 2.
2. Two conflicting readings of the focus-degradation threshold and binary impossibility of a shared call (lines 10, 14, 30, 54, 58) — Defect (`kb/reports/state/review/results/kb/theory/context-isolation-for-focus-conflicts-with-global-prioritization.md/semantic/underspecified-assertions.md`; `kb/reports/state/review/results/kb/theory/context-isolation-for-focus-conflicts-with-global-prioritization.md/kb/instructions/premise-decomposition-gate.md`; `kb/reports/state/review/results/kb/theory/context-isolation-for-focus-conflicts-with-global-prioritization.md/kb/instructions/composition-friction-gate.md`): the artifact's own wording supports Reading 1 — strict zero measurable focus degradation ("without degrading focus", lines 14, 30; "without eroding focus", line 54) — and Reading 2 — exceeding the task's usable-window feasibility ceiling ("usable attention budget", line 10; "fits inside one usable window", line 58). Under soft attention decay, Reading 1 forces a split whenever co-loading causes any focus dip, which is defeated by the case where mild focus loss inside the feasibility margin outperforms a split architecture's larger compression-misclassification or deep-context fallback costs; Reading 2 permits compact O(1) summaries on large workloads.
3. Observer-relative "scale-bearing local facts" tension at the execution-triage interface (lines 12, 32, 53) — Defect (`kb/reports/state/review/results/kb/theory/context-isolation-for-focus-conflicts-with-global-prioritization.md/kb/instructions/premise-decomposition-gate.md`; `kb/reports/state/review/results/kb/theory/context-isolation-for-focus-conflicts-with-global-prioritization.md/kb/instructions/critique-note.md`; `kb/reports/state/review/results/kb/theory/context-isolation-for-focus-conflicts-with-global-prioritization.md/kb/instructions/composition-friction-gate.md`): two statements sit in conflict—line 12 states that cross-boundary blast radius, external deadlines, and external reversibility depend on excluded state, yet line 32 assigns "scale-bearing local facts" to the isolated worker as purely task-internal judgments (and line 53 treats missed emergencies as worker omission of severe local detail). Case: an isolated worker refactoring a serialization helper verifies locally that changing JSON key order breaks nothing inside its module and does not flag it, unaware that an external billing check hashes raw JSON; logging every locally benign detail instead breaks triage compression.
4. Unattended stopping/redirection overclaim and motivating-example causal tensions (lines 18, 22-23, 37, 41, 54) — Defect (`kb/reports/state/review/results/kb/theory/context-isolation-for-focus-conflicts-with-global-prioritization.md/kb/instructions/composition-friction-gate.md`; `kb/reports/state/review/results/kb/theory/context-isolation-for-focus-conflicts-with-global-prioritization.md/kb/instructions/premise-decomposition-gate.md`; `kb/reports/state/review/results/kb/theory/context-isolation-for-focus-conflicts-with-global-prioritization.md/kb/instructions/critique-note.md`): (a) line 37 leaves diminishing-returns and global opportunity-cost stopping to triage while workers stop only on hard blockers or pre-injected stop rules, and line 54 leaves within-episode branch choices inside the worker, yet line 41 claims unbundling local stopping from immediate operator action addresses degraded stopping and redirection in unattended work—case: a mid-run tangent or debugging loop never triggers a hard blocker, so post-stop asynchronous decoupling cannot halt or redirect it; (b) line 23 attributes earnest low-value tangents to absent external competing work while conceding in its parenthetical that the already-loaded in-window primary task supplies no counterweight, and line 22's "either way" bridge over the juice-box/bleeding-finger example sits in tension with line 18's claim that isolated agents retain pretrained base-rate severity priors.
